memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “But those who wait on the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint. - Isaiah 40:31.

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
The Lord compares the life of those who wait for Him to an eagle. This is because the eagle does not rise by its own strength alone, but by the help of the wind. God did not choose the sparrow or the dove as an example here. He deliberately chose the eagle, because the life of an eagle teaches us deep spiritual truths.
An eagle does not keep flapping its wings continuously. It waits for the right wind, and when the current comes, it spreads its wings and rises higher. Likewise, believers are not called to struggle in their flesh. We are called to wait for the movement of the Spirit of God.
The eagle does not waste its strength on unnecessary movements. It waits for the right moment and uses that moment to soar high. In the same way, believers must wait wisely for the leading of the Holy Spirit. Waiting on the Lord is not weakness; it is spiritual training. When an eagle teaches its young ones to fly, it pushes them out of the nest. Though this may seem cruel, it is done so they can learn to fly. When the eaglet begins to fall, the mother eagle swoops down, catches it on her wings, and lifts it back up again.
 In the same way, at times God removes our comforts not to abandon us, but to lift us to higher levels. An eagle does not fear the storm and fly away from it. Instead, it rises above the storm and flies courageously. What frightens others becomes the very power that lifts the eagle higher. If you are waiting today, do not be discouraged. Waiting is not weakness; it is a season of strengthening.
The wind of the Holy Spirit is rising. Spread the wings of your faith. You are not called to crawl, you are called to fly.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: Waiting on the Lord is not laziness; it is active faith. Those who trust God’s timing receive strength from above. Where human strength ends, divine strength begins.

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, grant us the grace to wait on You in faith.
Renew our strength and lift us above all limitations.
Holy Spirit, strengthen us by Your grace and keep us from weariness. Help us to wait on the Lord and receive renewed strength. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Your season of struggle may be God’s season of training. God is not delaying you, He is preparing you to take you higher.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: Unlimited Power of Faith.
recommended_book.author: Bishop, David Oyedepo
recommended_book.quote: The Spirit of faith is the prompting of the Holy Spirit in stirring up the faith in you, when a challenge comes. The Spirit of faith comes on its own. It is the supernatural prompting of faith in you to confront challenges as they come.
